subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw first standardize canonical readiness only, or also adopt named hosting profiles and plugin/operator readiness composition as stable core contracts?
rationale: Current main does not expose these capabilities, and accepting them creates permanent cross-area product, support, configuration, API, and release obligations that document correctness alone cannot decide.

options.title: Approve readiness foundation first
options.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model and default local projection, then review named profiles and plugin composition as separate compatibility decisions.

options.title: Approve the full architecture
options.body: Commit to all proposed profiles, extension APIs, custom profile configuration, and release gates after exact-head runtime and upgrade proof.

options.title: Retain unprofiled readiness
options.body: Improve generally applicable readiness facts while leaving named hosting-posture composition to downstream hosts.

recommendation.title: Approve readiness foundation first
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model and default local projection, then review named profiles and plugin composition as separate compatibility decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the central Gateway, configuration, and plugin surfaces and was selected by the previous review cycle for the product-boundary decision.
